- When sentiment is consistently bearish (avg < 0.33) and supply net is negative, model tends to overestimate prices — apply downward bias correction.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5 days.
- If event count is high and bearish sentiment dominates, model overconfidently predicts upward trend — cap forecast growth at 2–3% per day unless sentiment flips.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when price volatility > 5% — adjust forecast to align with 14-day moving average if deviation > 3σ.
- When sentiment history shows repeated bearish swings (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model underreacts — add 0.5–1.0 to forecast for next 3 days to counteract lag.
- In high-event periods with net supply negative, model often misses downward pressure — add 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast if true outcome < 10% below 14-day avg.
